correctness.rationale: Attaching a fresh core by a bridge creates exactly two cross-square incidence types. A closed old neighborhood uses d_A(c)+1 distinct colors; the new rooted core contributes P_H(q)(q-d_H(a)-1)/(q(q-1)) by named-color symmetry. Each bridge endpoint accumulates the correct falling factorial, and the bridge-component contraction is a tree. A polynomial identity follows from infinitely many large palettes. Exact original-definition independent checks passed for all connected labelled graphs through 5 vertices at four palette sizes (3,088 cases), 340 random glued cases and two structural witnesses. Computational tests are corroborative only.

value.rationale: Determines exactly the entire ordinary distance-two coloring enumeration on every connected graph from its bridge-free components and local attachment degrees; it is not a fixed finite census. Shows the chromatic number is the max of delta+1 and core-square requirements and proves nonisomorphic bridge-tree arrangements may have identical square chromatic polynomials, including nonchordal cores. These are motivated structural invariants beyond minimum palette size.
